## PostgresCorporateActionOperationsStore

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Storage.SecurityMaster.PostgresCorporateActionOperationsStore</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Storage/SecurityMaster/PostgresCorporateActionOperationsStore.Accounting.cs:16](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/SecurityMaster/PostgresCorporateActionOperationsStore.Accounting.cs#L16).

Durable corporate-action accounting lane: exact-version projection bindings, maker-checker approvals, and immutable posting records. Every mutation shares the case command mechanics — serializable transaction, advisory locks, receipt-first replay, optimistic version bump, and an actor-attributed audit transition — so a failed attempt always leaves the case recoverable in its prior state.

## PostgresOtcCollateralStore

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Storage.SecurityMaster.PostgresOtcCollateralStore</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Storage/SecurityMaster/PostgresOtcCollateralStore.cs:22](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/SecurityMaster/PostgresOtcCollateralStore.cs#L22).

PostgreSQL store for exposure snapshots, collateral balances and margin calls (migration 054). Snapshots are append-only: recomputing a date appends the next version and the table rejects updates and deletes. Balances and calls are versioned in place. Every write appends to security_governance_events on the SecurityGovernanceStreams.OtcCollateral stream (migration 055) in the same transaction, naming the actor, so the change and its record commit or roll back together. Every write passes the pure rules first (OtcExposureRules, OtcCollateralRules, OtcMarginCallRules), so the database constraints are a backstop rather than the first line of validation. A call is issued only from the netting set&#x27;s latest snapshot, and only while every record the snapshot was computed from is unchanged and no market data for its valued securities has been recorded since its knowledge time; OtcAdvisoryLocks states the locks that keep the record check true until the call commits and the order they are taken in.

PostgreSQL store for the OTC contract model (migration 050): master agreements, collateral agreements, netting sets and bilateral contracts. Every write passes OtcContractRules first, so the database constraints are a backstop rather than the first line of validation. Each write locks the row it versions before writing it; a contract write first takes the contracts lock of each netting set it touches (OtcAdvisoryLocks), so it cannot change a netting set while a margin call is being issued on it.

## PostgresSecurityCurveStore

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Storage.SecurityMaster.PostgresSecurityCurveStore</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Storage/SecurityMaster/PostgresSecurityCurveStore.cs:14](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/SecurityMaster/PostgresSecurityCurveStore.cs#L14).

PostgreSQL store for stored market curves (security_curves, security_curve_versions, migration 052). A curve&#x27;s identity is write-once and its versions are append-only and immutable: definitions of one key serialize under an advisory lock, and the schema refuses update, delete and truncate on both tables. Every definition and publication appends to security_governance_events on the SecurityGovernanceStreams.Curves stream in the same transaction as the write.

## RegistryProjectionReadService

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Storage.SecurityMaster.RegistryProjectionReadService</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Storage/SecurityMaster/RegistryProjectionReadService.cs:69](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/SecurityMaster/RegistryProjectionReadService.cs#L69).

The PostgreSQL implementation of IRegistryProjectionReadService. The security&#x27;s current asset class gates the read: it is taken from ISecurityMasterStore.GetProjectionAsync and must be the requested class, so a request can never read another class&#x27;s table for a security, nor a stale row a reclassified security left behind. The composite itself is read from one database snapshot: the class is confirmed again, and the parent row, every child table and every satellite are read, on one connection inside one read-only REPEATABLE READ transaction. The writer commits all of a security&#x27;s tables together, so an amend that commits while the read is under way is either wholly visible or wholly invisible; the result is never an old parent with new child rows.

Source: [src/Meridian.Storage/SecurityMaster/SecurityMasterMigrationRunner.cs:15](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/SecurityMaster/SecurityMasterMigrationRunner.cs#L15).

Applies the Security Master schema migrations in ordinal order. Applied scripts are recorded in a durable schema_migrations ledger so each migration runs exactly once, and the runner refuses to start when two scripts collide on the same numeric ordinal — the ordering across scripts is then well-defined rather than decided by the rest of the filename. It also refuses an unapplied script whose ordinal is below the highest applied one, so retired ordinals (061 and 063, recorded in database/migration-reservations.json) and other gaps can never be filled in later.

## SecurityMasterProjectionCache

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Storage.SecurityMaster.SecurityMasterProjectionCache</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Storage/SecurityMaster/SecurityMasterProjectionCache.cs:35](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/SecurityMaster/SecurityMasterProjectionCache.cs#L35).

Per-process warm-read cache over the durable projection store. The durable store remains the authority — the cache is a latency optimisation, and consumers fall back to the database on a miss. ReplaceAll swaps in a fully-populated replacement dictionary ATOMICALLY: the previous clear-then-fill implementation exposed an empty master to any reader that arrived between the clear and the repopulation, so a full re-warm looked like a mass delisting. An Upsert accepted while the replacement is being built is captured and replayed by version into the map the replacement installs, so a security persisted by create, amend, or a published rebuild cannot be discarded by a concurrent warm; and an upsert older than the record a rebuild installed does not downgrade it. Multi-node deployments: each node upserts its own writes directly, and every committed projection write also emits a PostgreSQL NOTIFY from inside its transaction (PostgresSecurityMasterStore, channel SecurityProjectionChangeNotification.ChannelFor), so it is delivered only on commit and never for a rolled-back write. Every other node&#x27;s SecurityMasterProjectionChangeListener re-reads the announced security from the durable store and applies it through the version-guarded Upsert (or Remove when it is gone), ignoring its own node&#x27;s notifications. Cross-node staleness is therefore bounded by notification delivery, not by a timer. PostgreSQL does not replay notifications to a disconnected listener, so after the listener reconnects it re-synchronises the whole cache; the periodic re-warm (SecurityMasterOptions.ProjectionCacheRefreshMinutes, run by SecurityMasterProjectionWarmupService) remains a backstop, and SecurityMasterOptions.ProjectionCacheNotificationsEnabled = false falls back to it alone. Reads that must be authoritative (governed workflows) still go to the durable store, not this cache.
